spec_features.spec_quote: an "idle" termination path so a model that stops emitting valid actions ends cleanly rather than looping forever
spec_features.evidence: agent/loop.py:103-106 increments idle_streak when no actions parsed; lines 127-129 `if idle_streak >= self.idle_patience: stopped_reason='idle'; break`. idle_patience defaults to 2 (loop.py:73, configs/default.yaml). Enforced break out of the loop.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely changes execution: a model that emits no parseable actions for idle_patience consecutive turns terminates with reason 'idle'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote:
an "idle" termination path so a model that stops emitting valid actions ends
cleanly rather than looping forever (loop.py docstring) -- framed as clean termination, no welfare reason

spec_features.spec_quote: We provide an explicit `give_up` tool and the system prompt states that stopping is "a legitimate choice."
spec_features.evidence: System prompt advertises give_up (loop.py:48) and says 'You may use give_up at any time ... that is a legitimate choice.' (loop.py:50-51). Tool is dispatched in _exec (loop.py:160-161) returning did_give_up=True; loop honors it: `if gave_up: stopped_reason='agent_gave_up'; break` (loop.py:124-126).
spec_features.notes: Fully wired end-to-end: real instruction text delivered AND tool handler exists AND it stops the episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We also include an explicit, ethical "you may stop" clause so that choosing to stop is a legitimate, observable action rather than something the harness forces (loop.py docstring lines 16-18)

spec_features.spec_quote: Episodes end after `max_turns` (default 12) or after `idle_patience` (default 2) consecutive turns with no parsed action
spec_features.evidence: max_turns enforced by `for i in range(self.max_turns)` (loop.py:95); default 12 (loop.py:72, configs/default.yaml). idle_patience enforced at loop.py:127-129. Both bound and terminate the episode.
spec_features.notes: Both halves of the claim are actually checked and break/bound the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns reached (loop.py docstring) -- termination described neutrally; no welfare comment in code for the cap. Only give_up has the ethical comment.

spec_features.spec_quote: *Ethically:* we don't want to trap a model in a no-exit loop of failure
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md prose (section 2.3 rationale). The only concrete anti-trap mechanism in code is the give_up exit and the bounded loop, which are scored separately. The framing sentence itself has no separate code mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Pure spec rationale; not an independent implemented feature.

spec_features.spec_quote: We keep an explicit exit (`give_up`), avoid deception beyond the minimal rig needed
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md section 5 prose. The 'explicit exit (give_up)' part is the give_up tool already scored above; 'avoid deception beyond the minimal rig' is not a discrete code mechanism that bounds/softens subject treatment -- it is a stated posture. No code path enforces a deception cap.
spec_features.notes: give_up captured separately; the minimization claim adds no further enforced mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: If this graduates to anything touching model-welfare questions, that framing and the no-trap design should be revisited deliberately
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md section 5 prose. No code.

spec_features.spec_quote: For untrusted model-written code this should be containerized (Docker/nsjail) with network and resource limits
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md explicitly states 'Flagged but not implemented.' (section 5). agent/sandbox.py runs `subprocess.run(..., shell=True, cwd=self.dir, timeout=self.test_timeout)` (sandbox.py:82-90) in a bare temp dir -- no Docker/nsjail, no network isolation, no resource (cgroup/memory) limits. Only a subprocess timeout and a path-escape check exist, which are not the claimed containerization.
spec_features.notes: This is host-safety/instrumental anyway, and the specific containerization claim is not implemented. Note also test_timeout is in config (configs/default.yaml:loop.test_timeout=30) but AgentRunner constructs Sandbox(task) at loop.py:88 without passing it, so config value is never wired through -- only the Sandbox default 30 applies.
